placement.detail: Fowl confinement/enclosure must be kept sanitary and avoid nuisance, vectors and odor. §14-17 itself supplies no lot-line setback. The §14-16(d) 100-ft human-dwelling proximity test governs small/large LIVESTOCK and cannot automatically be applied to gallinaceous fowl.

max.section: Irving Code §6-62(a)(1)-(2)
max.detail: On <=1 acre: more than 25 chickens total (including rooster) prohibited, and at most one rooster if >=6 hens. >1 acre rooster/hen ratio addressed but no total flock max established by cited section.

roosters.section: Irving Code §6-62(a),(d)
roosters.detail: <=1 acre one rooster only with >=6 hens; >1 acre no more than one rooster per six hens. Special exhibition, government and research exceptions only if conditions met.

permit.section: Irving current Animal Code §6-62(c)(1), (d); Ordinance 2021-10468
permit.detail: Chicken enclosure must comply with applicable city building and zoning law; extraordinary permitted animal exhibition under (d) is separate. §6-62 does NOT state that every routine coop is permit-free, nor does this isolated clause resolve routine keeping license or exact building approval.

placement.detail: Coop >=25 ft from occupied/intended habitation structure on OTHER person's land, roofed >=1 sq ft roost space per chicken + outdoor >=10 sq ft per chicken; separate building/zoning standards apply.

max.section: §22.14 Fowl
max.detail: Four female fowl older than one month, combined domestic fowl

roosters.section: §22.14 Fowl
roosters.detail: Roosters and male peafowl prohibited

permit.detail: Zoning/building-permit coverage not resolved by reviewed city ordinance

placement.detail: 30 ft to other dwelling and 5 ft from adjacent residential-zoned property for pens/runs

max.section: McKinney Animal Control FAQ: Am I allowed to have chickens in city limits?
max.detail: Up to twelve hens in proper enclosure; FAQ does not establish a universal parcel building setback.

roosters.section: McKinney Animal Control FAQ: Am I allowed to have chickens in city limits?
roosters.detail: No roosters of any kind permitted by city animal guidance.

max.section: Denton City Animal Services FAQ: Can I keep chickens? / §6-26
max.detail: Up to eight hens per single residential neighborhood property; zoning and sanitation rules remain.

roosters.section: Denton City Animal Services FAQ: Can I keep chickens?
roosters.detail: Roosters prohibited on residential parcels smaller than one acre. Larger parcels not blanket approved: check ordinance/zoning.

permit.section: Denton Building Safety Accessory Structures (Residential), permit exemptions and zoning note; current 2026 website
permit.detail: General accessory structures require permits; 1-story detached tool/storage shed/playhouse and SIMILAR uses no more than 200sqft and no electrical/plumbing/HVAC do not require construction permit; zoning/land development still apply. Whether particular poultry coop qualifies needs city inspection; separate poultry-keeping permits unresolved.

placement.section: Denton City Animal Services FAQ: Can I keep chickens? / §6-26
placement.detail: Enclosures at least 150 ft from a residence, business/commercial office, school, hospital or nursing home, per official city FAQ; check exact reference geometry and city zoning.

max.detail: The phrase 'fewer than six' is a permit EXCEPTION for pets, not a six-bird universal legal maximum; higher flock with permit's veterinary officer discretion, subject to zoning.

roosters.section: El Paso Code §7.24.020(B)(1) (current municipal code)
roosters.detail: Up to 3 roosters wherever fowl otherwise allowed; max three is not unconditional rooster permission in every residential zone.

permit.detail: Permit ordinarily required for six or more birds/rabbits except farm-ranch/stockyard-stable zones, household pets <6 exempt. Application inspection and veterinary officer conditions, potential revocation.

placement.detail: Only animals SUBJECT TO FOWL PERMIT: secure enclosure >=30 ft from another private RESIDENCE, apartment/hotel/church/school etc; special alley+solid wall allows 20-ft; vet may waive after nuisance/safety review. Not property line or automatic for <6 pets.

roosters.section: NYC Health Code §161.19(a)
roosters.detail: Live roosters prohibited in New York City except specified authorized slaughterhouses or Health Code §161.01(a) exemptions; city's Urban Agriculture FAQ confirms ordinary backyard hens are permitted, roosters are not.

permit.section: NYC Urban Agriculture FAQ and separate commercial Health Code §161.19
permit.detail: NYC allows backyard HENS and prohibits ROOSTERS. Commercial live-poultry market permits are a DIFFERENT business use, not automatic backyard licence requirements; individual coop structural/zoning approvals remain undetermined.

max.section: Minneapolis §63.90(g), (h)(1)
max.detail: Chicken permit Tier I 1–6 HENS, Tier II 7–15, Tier III 16–30. Normal residential coop SIX fowl only; >6 requires explicit MACC APPROVAL and possibly extra conditions. Tier III NOT automatic 30 birds.

roosters.section: Backyard chickens and other fowl / Annual Fowl Permit Application Fees (updated 2026-07-06)
roosters.detail: City's official fee schedule lists a separate $110 rooster permit category. This does not guarantee permission at an address; neighbor consent, zoning approval, education and inspection remain required.

permit.section: Backyard chickens and other fowl / Application process (updated 2026-07-06)
permit.detail: Fowl permit MUST be approved before birds are bought; neighbor consent, approved course, zoning approval and animal-control inspection required; permit renewed annually. Building permissions separate.

placement.detail: Residential coop/run must be ≥20 ft from a HABITABLE BUILDING on an ADJACENT property (not lot line), entirely REAR of principal dwelling, screened from neighboring residences, zoning compliant.

max.section: City of Madison Chicken License: Regulations for Keeping Chickens, bullet 5
max.detail: Up to eight chickens as accessory use on lots containing up to four dwelling units and at qualified school, daycare or museum sites.

roosters.section: City of Madison Chicken License: Regulations for Keeping Chickens, bullet 2
roosters.detail: No roosters permitted.

permit.section: City of Madison Chicken License: registration, application and renewal sections
permit.detail: City chicken license required, apply within 30 days of acquisition, renew by Jan 1; Wisconsin DATCP livestock premises registration also required; zoning/building permits not automatically waived.

placement.section: City of Madison Chicken License: Regulations for Keeping Chickens, bullets 7-8
placement.detail: Chickens must stay within a covered or fenced enclosure; enclosure at least 25 ft from any residential structure on an adjacent lot (not measured from property boundary).

max.section: Indianapolis §743-306(W)(1)-(4), Table 743-306-3
max.detail: Eligible owner/resident of single-/two-family home may keep up to 12 combined adult chickens, quail, pigeons and ducks without personal livestock license; adult means 8+ months and counts combined, not by species.

roosters.section: Indianapolis §743-306(W)(5)
roosters.detail: One rooster per lot maximum; bird remains fully enclosed between dusk and dawn.

permit.section: Indianapolis §743-306(W)(3)-(4), Chapter 838
permit.detail: Personal livestock license not required for qualifying category-one poultry within standard cap; larger numbers or special lots require valid license; structure/building permits remain independent.

placement.detail: No front-yard coop, pen, roost, shelter or exercise area. Applicable zoning district setbacks, fencing and containment requirements apply; no single universal numeric setback is stated.

max.section: Raleigh Home Gardens guidance, updated 2026-07-13

roosters.section: Raleigh UDO §6.6.1(B)(2)(h)(iii)
roosters.detail: Raleigh prohibits animal raising in RESIDENTIAL community gardens; in eligible NONRESIDENTIAL COMMUNITY GARDENS chicken keeping max 1 per 1000sqft, max10, and NO ROOSTERS. Scope is community gardens, not all home backyards.

permit.section: Raleigh City Planning How to Start a Community Garden, updated 2026-07-15
permit.detail: A community garden requires a Tier One planning review before permit issuance. §6.6.1(B)(2)(h) bars residential-district community-garden animals. Does NOT establish permit exemption or zoning approval for an ordinary backyard coop.

placement.detail: Eligible NONRESIDENTIAL community-garden coops must stand at least 25 ft from ANY PROPERTY LINE. This does NOT establish setbacks/permission for all residential backyard enclosures.
